content: Always connect price discussion back to demonstrated value using a spin_need_payoff question to prevent price-only focus.
When customer mentions a competitor device (e.g., Mi Pad 5 Pro), immediately probe for pain points to strengthen your product's differentiation.
Use specific local details (exact store, address, warranty center name) to build trust and remove last objections.
In in-store demos, invite physical handling (hold the device, compare weight) to engage more senses and increase ownership feeling.
After confirming warranty and price, use an assumptive close with a specific next step (e.g., 'Which installment tenure?') to move to closing.

name: Live Demo Value Anchoring
condition: When customer shows interest but asks about price or warranty before seeing full value.
example: After customer asks price, say: 'Let me first show you how it handles [their use case]—then we can talk about the investment.' Then run a quick demo and ask: 'How would that performance change your daily workflow?'

name: Local Specificity Trust Builder
condition: When customer asks about warranty or service locations.
example: Instead of saying 'we have centers in your city', say: 'The authorized center at [exact street name, district] is just [distance] from here. I can show you on the map.' This leverages local knowledge to build trust.

name: Assumptive Close with Installment Options
condition: After all objections are resolved and customer shows buying signals.
example: Say: 'Great choice! Let me confirm your order. Which installment plan works best for you—6, 9, or 12 months?' This assumes the sale and gives a limited choice to close.

objection: Customer asks about price without seeing value
rebuttal_template: I understand price is important. Before we talk numbers, let me show you how the [product] handles [specific task you care about]—I think you'll be impressed. [Proceed with live demo].

objection: Customer compares with competitor's cheaper model
rebuttal_template: I see you're considering [competitor model]. Let's do a quick side-by-side test here—open the same app on both devices and see which one loads faster and stays cooler. [Invite customer to hold both].

Here's the official warranty card—it covers parts and labor for one year at any authorized center. Let me show you the list of centers in [city]; the one at [specific address] is just [distance] from here. [Point to physical map or show on phone].
